Customer (Linda Douglas): Can you explain how the equalization plan works out my monthly amount?
Agent (Zanele Radebe): Hi Linda Douglas, Zanele Radebe here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Linda Douglas): If the point of this plan is predictable payments, why does it keep moving?

Customer (Linda Douglas): This is the third time this year my equalized amount has changed on me.
Agent (Zanele Radebe): When did you first join the equalization plan?
Customer (Linda Douglas): About two years ago, when we moved in.
Agent (Zanele Radebe): Did you get a notice before the amount changed?
Customer (Linda Douglas): No. I found out when the payment came out.
Agent (Zanele Radebe): Would you rather stay on the plan or go back to regular billing?

Agent (Zanele Radebe): The plan recalculates twice a year against your rolling usage average, and this adjustment reflects higher usage than last year's estimate — I've set up an email alert so you'll get advance notice before the next recalculation instead of finding out on the bill.
Customer (Linda Douglas): Will it change again without warning?
Agent (Zanele Radebe): The next review is in six months, and you'll get an email two weeks before it.
Customer (Linda Douglas): And the catch-up amount?
Agent (Zanele Radebe): I've spread it over your remaining months so there's no lump sum.
Agent (Zanele Radebe): To recap: the catch-up is spread over the rest of the plan year, and you'll get an email two weeks before the next review.
Customer (Linda Douglas): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Zanele Radebe): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Customer (Ryan Wilson): This bill says 'estimated read' again. Can someone come and read my meter?
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Hi Ryan Wilson, Vusi Jacobs here — let me pull that up.

Customer (Ryan Wilson): Sure, it's the house on the account, and the bill's in my name.
Customer (Ryan Wilson): If the estimate is wrong, how does the correction actually happen on a future bill?
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Can you see the meter from outside, or is it behind a gate?
Customer (Ryan Wilson): It's behind the back gate, and the dog's out there during the day.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): How many estimated bills have you had in a row?

Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Would a self-read reminder by email work for you?

Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): When our reader can't reach the meter, the bill is estimated from your past usage for the same months.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): I've scheduled an actual field read for your next cycle and shown you how to submit a self-read online in the meantime, so this month's estimate will be corrected against the real number once it's read.
Customer (Ryan Wilson): So I'll get the overcharge back?
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): It's credited automatically on the next bill once the actual read is in.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Customer (Ryan Wilson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
